scholarships.title: HFA Research and Training Grants Programme (Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology)
scholarships.official_source: Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology (HFA-ESC)

eligibility: Under 40 years of age as of the application deadline
HFA Member or Fellow of the HFA; membership is required to be eligible

Hold an MD but not yet hold a post defined as permanent, senior staff or consultant, and demonstrate expertise in heart failure through examination, practice, scientific publication or an abstract presentation at a national or international meeting; OR
Hold a PhD, DPhil degree or equivalent, or have submitted a thesis before starting the funded research period
Project to be conducted in an ESC member country outside the applicant's own country
Project proposal prepared in collaboration with the proposed host centre for a minimum of three months
Applicants preferably apply to an HFA ICARe-HF Accredited Centre
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under 40, be an HFA member or Fellow, hold an MD without a permanent, senior staff or consultant post with demonstrated heart failure expertise, or hold a PhD or have submitted a thesis, and must carry out their project in an ESC member country outside their own for at least three months.
benefits: EUR 2,500 per month for the duration of the exchange period
Maximum grant of EUR 10,000 per award
Funding to carry out research in a partner laboratory or clinical centre and to learn new procedures
coverage: EUR 2,500 per month for the duration of the exchange period
Maximum grant of EUR 10,000 per award
Funding to carry out research in a partner laboratory or clinical centre and to learn new procedures
requirements: Project proposal prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor
Confirmation documents from the current head of department or supervisor and from the future host supervisor
Submission through the My ESC account
documents: CV covering postgraduate career and present employment, previous clinical cardiology training, research experience, academic record, and publications in refereed journals with journal titles, page numbers and co-author names
Document completed by the current head of department or supervisor
Candidate project description prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor
Document completed by the future supervisor
Letter of recommendation, for example from a head of department or supervisor
application_method: Log in to the My ESC account and submit the application through the applications section, selecting 'New Grant Application' and then the HFA grants programme
The application form is visible only during the application period and only if the eligibility criteria are met
existing.selection_notes: Applications are graded from one to five by an HFA-composed task force against published weightings: feasibility and importance of the project with an assessment of sustained benefits for local and global cardiovascular disease reduction, 50%; candidate's profile, meaning optimal career stage and achievements so far, 20%; citizenship or permanent residence in a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank, 20%; and quality of the host centre in the research or training field and its track record in the topic, 10%. Results are announced in December of the application year, and accepted exchange periods must start by May of the following year.
existing.best_fit: Heart failure investigators and cardiology trainees under 40 who hold an HFA membership and want a three-month or longer research or clinical training placement at a centre in another ESC member country.
existing.notes: Grant recipients must submit a report on the work at the end of the project period and inform the HFA of the appointment they propose to undertake. Any publication arising from the grant must acknowledge the Heart Failure Association of the ESC in the form of an HFA Grant, and one print-off of each publication must be provided to the HFA.
existing.duration: Minimum three months; the grant is paid at EUR 2,500 per month up to a maximum of EUR 10,000
existing.deadline_display: 30 September (annual close; the 2026 call closed on 30 September 2026)
existing.program_type: Professional association research and training grant with mandatory mobility
